title: Tufts sues after order to reinstate professor fired for sexual activity in his office
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Education A student reported the professor to Tufts administration last year after they heard “sexual noises” coming from his office.

Suzanne Kreiter/The Boston Globe By Abby Patkin October 26, 2026 | 4:37 PM 3 minutes to read Tufts University is seeking to overturn an arbitrator’s decision reinstating a professor who was fired last year after he admitted to engaging in sexual activity in his office — a tryst overheard by one of his students.

Filed earlier this month and first reported by The Tufts Daily, the university’s federal lawsuit asks a judge to vacate the arbitration award issued under a collective bargaining agreement with Service Employees International Union Local 509, the union representing theater professor Ted Simpson and other Tufts instructors.

title: Two Mass. biotech companies plan to cut about half their workers
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Business Fractyl Health will focus on maintaining weight loss after GLP-1 drugs, while EyePoint will prioritize a treatment for diabetes-related vision loss.

Two Massachusetts biotech companies announced plans last week to cut roughly half their workforces as they narrow their focuses to experimental treatments for weight management and diabetes-related vision loss.

Burlington-based Fractyl Health announced a 45% workforce reduction, which would eliminate about 45 jobs if its staffing remains at the level reported earlier this year, while Watertown-based EyePoint plans to lay off 105 workers, according to a notice filed with the state.
